Notes and Source

Quick Start

The initial view is country bubbles and global crosses. Only countries contributing >0.5% of total global emissions are shown (not all available countries).

Emissions share is the main variable along the horizontal axis, meaning the share of regional total anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions from the category – initially an emissions sector – on the vertical axis.

Bubble colour is 5-year absolute change in emissions share (green up, red down), bubble size is absolute emissions (megatonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent). Either of these variables can also be selected as the main variable.

Hover over a point to see its details (or select on a touch screen).

Zoom charts with horizontal axes by dragging horizontally on the chart pane (or separate two fingers on touch screens). On desktop, pan left and right when zoomed in using the shift key.

Configure main variable (including which greenhouse gases to include), categories, chart type (which also include share, time series and map) and display options from the menu, top right.

Change year and select a region using controls below the chart.

Highlight and toggle visibility of categories using legend at top of chart.

Category Definitions

Sector categories are summarised by the source as follows:

Power – power and heat generation plants (public & autoproducers).

Fuel Production – production, transformation and refining of fuels.

Ind. Combustion – combustion for industrial manufacturing.

Ind. Processes – industrial processes e.g. emissions from the production of cement, iron and steel, aluminium, chemicals, solvents, etc.

Transport – mobile combustion (road & rail & ship & aviation).

Agriculture – agricultural soils, crop residues burning, enteric fermentation, manure management, indirect nitrous oxide emissions from agriculture.

Buildings – small scale non-industrial stationary combustion.

Waste – solid waste disposal and waste water treatment.

Two groupings of the above categories are also available:

Energy Supply – combines Power and Fuel Production.

Industry – combines Ind. Combustion and Ind. Processes.

Land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF) emissions are not included. There is an alternative explorer that includes LULUCF.

Carbon dioxide (excluding biomass/biofuel combustion), nitrous oxide, methane and certain fluorinated gases (shown as f-gases), are the greenhouse gases included.

Note that cement sucks up carbon dioxide over time; this cement carbonation sink is not currently included.

Emissions of different gases are aggregated and displayed using 100-year Global Warming Potential (GWP) values from the fifth assessment report (AR5) of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). This is the method used by the source, though it makes the GWP values slightly dated (AR6 values exist). However, the difference is often minor – a 0.3 Gt (~0.5%) difference on the global total is suggested by the UN’s Emission Gap Report 2024; the uncertainty ranges on the total are more than an order of magnitude greater than this. Emissions Gap Report 2024 | UNEP – UN Environment Programme.

Sector and gas categories are defined more precisely in the relevant source, see below.

Source

Visualisation by Climateninja.org.

Data were taken from:

EDGAR (Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research) Community GHG Database, a collaboration between the European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC), the International Energy Agency (IEA), and comprising IEA-EDGAR CO2, EDGAR CH4, EDGAR N2O, EDGAR F-GASES version EDGAR_2026_GHG (2026) European Commission, JRC (Datasets). EDGAR – The Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research (europa.eu).

Definitions of sectors (and gases) used can be found in the pdf report located on the same page as the above EDGAR link – Crippa et al., GHG emissions of all world countries, Publications Office of the European Union, Luxembourg, 2026, doi:10.2760/7717504, JRC147815.

GDP (used for emissions per GDP PPP): World Bank, World Development Indicators, GDP, PPP (constant 2021 international $), NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD, licensed under CC BY 4.0 – the same series EDGAR uses. Where the World Bank has no 2025 value, 2025 is the 2024 value grown by the real GDP growth of the IMF World Economic Outlook (IMF DataMapper; source: IMF, used under the IMF copyright and usage terms), as EDGAR does. Lumped EDGAR regions are sums of their World Bank countries. Where the World Bank has no data (e.g. Taiwan, Venezuela, North Korea, Cuba, and some early years), GDP is derived from EDGAR’s own figures (GHG emissions ÷ GHG per GDP). Changes: World Bank values converted to billion USD and aggregated. Population (used for emissions per capita) is derived from EDGAR’s figures (GHG emissions ÷ GHG per capita), so per-capita values match EDGAR’s.

Map geometry: Made with Natural Earth – free vector and raster map data @ naturalearthdata.com (1:50m Admin 0 – Countries, public domain). Boundaries are shown for data display only and do not imply any position on disputed territories; some EDGAR regions combine several territories (e.g. Italy, San Marino and the Holy See), which are then coloured with the same value.

This offline version is built using Apache ECharts (Apache License 2.0), converted from the original Highcharts version at climateninja.org/emissions-explorer.
